cited_evidence.text: AbstractHfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy has wide application prospects as a biomedical material, and the use of laser additive manufacturing can solve the forming problems faced by the alloy. In view of the characteristics of the one-time forming of additive manufacturing methods, it is necessary to develop non-mechanical processing modification methods. In this paper, deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) is first applied to the modification of a HEA with BCC structure, then the post-processing method of DCT is combined with laser melting deposition (LMD) technology to successfully realize the coordinated improvement of forming and strength–ductility synergistic improvement in lightweight Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr alloy. The final tensile strength of the alloy after DCT treatment is 25% higher than that of the as-cast alloy and 11% higher than that of the as-deposited alloy, and the elongation is increased by 48% and 10%, respectively. In addition, DCT also achieves induced phase transition without additional deformation.Keywords: laser melting deposition, high entropy alloy, deep cryogenic treatment, 3D printing, defects, strength–ductility synergistic improvement

At present, the casting forming of HEAs is facing some problems due to their high melt viscosity, and laser additive manufacturing (AM) technology can effectively solve this problem [,,]. Laser melting deposition (LMD) technology has high energy density and complex-shape-forming ability, which can solve the problem of HEA forming and accumulate thermal stress in as-deposited alloy samples []. At the same time, deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) has been gradually applied as a method to uniformly aggravate the residual stress generated by LMD, and remarkable results have been achieved []. In previous studies, the DCT method has often been used to modify FCC structural metals by constructing twins [,]. In this paper, LMD forming and DCT treatment were carried out on the previously designed lower-density Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr alloy in which the atoms of Hf and Ta are 25% of the atoms of other elements, in order to achieve a strength–ductility synergistic improvement by increasing the internal stress and lattice distortion so as to make up for the performance degradation caused by the decrease in density compared with the equiatomic ratio system. decision.trend: Research has been focused on improving the properties of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) through additive manufacturing (AM) processes. Earlier studies have explored the synthesis of HEAs via powder bed fusion (PBF) and laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) processes, and have investigated the effects of processing conditions on the microstructure and properties of HEAs. More recent studies have demonstrated the potential of deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) and directed energy deposition (DED) for improving the strength and ductility of HEAs. The trend suggests a shift towards optimizing AM processes and post-processing treatments to achieve high-performance HEAs.
decision.unsolved: Despite the progress made in AM of HEAs, there are still challenges to be addressed, such as reducing fabrication-induced defects, improving dimensional precision, and enhancing mechanical integrity. Additionally, the effects of nonequilibrium chemical short-range order (SRO) on the properties of HEAs are not yet fully understood, and further research is needed to explore the potential of SRO for tailoring materials properties.
decision.why: Based on the trend of research, DCT has shown promise in improving the strength and ductility of HEAs. By applying DCT to additively manufactured HEA components, it may be possible to reduce fabrication-induced defects and improve mechanical integrity, while also enhancing dimensional precision. This approach aligns with the goal of improving the properties of HEAs through optimized AM processes and post-processing treatments.
